fourthwall.label: Fourthwall
fourthwall.intro: Fourthwall hosts the shop, takes payment, and prints and ships catalog products. We supply the art, branding, and prices.

steps.title: Create a Fourthwall account
steps.body: Sign up and name your shop We — The Nameless. YHWH can be the public shopkeeper. Use your real business details for billing and verification. You’re ready when the shop dashboard opens.

steps.title: Design your first shirt
steps.body: In Products, create a catalog listing and choose a print-on-demand tee. Upload original artwork in the designer and check placement, colors, sizes, and mockups. Save the first listing. You can use the same process for stickers, mugs, and posters.

steps.title: Set a retail price
steps.body: Check the base production cost for each garment and variant. Subtract production, payment fees, shipping you cover, and other per-order costs from your retail price to estimate what each sale contributes. Check the actual fees and save prices you’re comfortable with.

steps.title: Design the storefront
steps.body: In the site designer, set the shop name, theme, logo, colors, description, and policies. Preview the public site. To use a branded subdomain such as shop.wethenameless.com, add it under Settings → Domains and enter the DNS records Fourthwall gives you at your DNS host. Wait for the domain to verify.

steps.title: Set up payouts and billing
steps.body: As the shop owner, open Settings → Billing and payouts and follow the payout setup. Enter the requested identity, business, tax, and banking details on the provider’s site. Add a billing method there if required. Check the dashboard for any outstanding verification requests.

steps.title: Order and inspect a sample
steps.body: Use Place order in the Fourthwall dashboard to buy a sample. Inspect the print, fit, artwork placement, and packaging. Check shipping cost and delivery time before promoting the design.

steps.title: Publish the shop
steps.body: Set the site status to Live and make the product listings visible. Copy the shop address from the dashboard. Open it in a private browser window and check that a visitor can see the storefront and products.

shopify.label: Printify + Shopify
shopify.intro: Shopify runs the listings, checkout, payments, and customer orders. Printify makes and ships the products. We own the artwork, branding, pricing, policies, and merchant obligations.
shopify.launch: Launch the store from Shopify admin and remove its storefront password. Confirm that visitors can browse it in a private browser window.

steps.title: Create a Shopify account
steps.body: Create a Shopify store for We — The Nameless and enter your business details in Shopify. Review current subscription prices and choose a plan that can publish an online store when you’re ready to launch.

steps.title: Create a Printify account
steps.body: Sign up and open the Printify dashboard. The free plan is enough to start. Compare the current paid plans once actual order volumes give you a way to judge the production discounts.

steps.title: Connect Printify to Shopify
steps.body: Install the official Printify app in Shopify and sign into Printify from it. Verify the connection under My Stores. Published products and variants go to Shopify. Orders come back to Printify for approval and fulfillment, and tracking returns to Shopify. Review your variant availability and order approval settings.

steps.title: Design your first shirt
steps.body: Choose a tee and a print provider in Printify’s catalog. Compare garment, print locations, size and color availability, and shipping to your target markets. Upload original artwork, choose sizes and colors, and preview the placement and mockups.

steps.title: Publish products to Shopify
steps.body: Publish the product from Printify to your connected store. In Shopify Products, check the images, description, variants, prices, shipping profile, Active status, and Online Store availability. Preview the listing as a shopper.

steps.title: Compare retail prices and margins
steps.body: Calculate contribution per sale after production, shipping you cover, payment fees, and other variable costs. Account for subscription costs when comparing profits at your actual volume. Use comparable garments, print placement, and destinations when comparing with Fourthwall.

steps.title: Make the shop look like We — The Nameless
steps.body: Open Online Store → Themes and preview a theme with your logo, colors, type, and product images. Check desktop and phone layouts before publishing it. A custom frontend using Shopify’s Storefront API can come later.

steps.title: Choose a public domain
steps.body: Keep the Shopify-hosted address or connect a custom domain in Settings → Domains. Apply Shopify’s DNS records at your DNS host and wait for the connection and HTTPS to be ready. Give this shop a distinct hostname if both stores are live.

steps.title: Set up payments, shipping, taxes, and policies
steps.body: In Shopify Settings, configure payments and payouts, shipping zones and rates, taxes, and your customer-facing return and privacy policies. Check that Printify can fulfill the destinations you list and set its billing method separately. Verify both dashboards and handle any tax, filing, or customer-service obligations for your business.

steps.title: Test checkout and fulfillment
steps.body: Use Shopify’s test payment mode to check checkout, order records, shipping rates, and tax. Turn test mode off afterward. Use a Printify sample to check print quality and delivery. If you need to verify the full Shopify-to-Printify handoff, review approval settings and place a controlled real order, which can incur production and shipping charges.
